clue.text: The end of play is baffling

definitions.meaning: in cricket, ... is the close of a day's play, when the ... are pulled up
to stump someone is to baffle them, so 'is baffling' is the verb in the third person

explanation.surface: Someone finds the way a game finished hard to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the cricket term for close of play, and the verb meaning to perplex or puzzle someone.

clue.text: Rupert met fantastic musician

indicators.note: fantastic in the sense of fanciful or wild signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rupert has met a wonderful musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpeter is a player of the trumpet, a brass instrument.

clue.text: Bond's boss at the office, cringing at psychic's skill?

parts.note: M is James Bond's superior in the novels and films
in means at work, as in 'is she in today?'
dreading means fearing, shrinking from

explanation.surface: James Bond's chief at work, shrinking from a psychic's abilities.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychics claim the ability to know others' thoughts telepathically.

clue.text: Charm, first of pieces put in auction

indicators.note: put in means inserted, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: to auction something is to sell it

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A lucky charm, the first lot, is entered into a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm is a magic spell or incantation.

clue.text: Imagine, my dear, a rum after end of round

indicators.note: the anagram is placed after the single letter, so that letter leads
the end of a word is its final letter, here the last letter of round
rum here is the adjective meaning odd or strange, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone invites their dear to picture a glass of rum after a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but signals that MY DEAR A is rearranged to AYDREAM; 'end of round' gives D, which 'after' puts first.
explanation.definitionFit: To daydream is to indulge in fanciful thought, a synonym of imagining things.

clue.text: 'Hello, Goodbye' as performed in 'South Pacific'

parts.note: the Hawaiian greeting serves for both hello and goodbye, and Hawaii is in the Pacific; the titles of a Beatles song and a musical are a decoy

explanation.surface: The Beatles song being sung in the Rodgers and Hammerstein musical.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hawaiian word is used both as a greeting and as a farewell in the Pacific islands.

clue.text: Reserved reduced object

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: demure means modest and reserved

explanation.surface: A shy, shrunken item.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection, so it is the verb object.

clue.text: Former partner has taken up painting more

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: painting is art

explanation.surface: An ex has started painting more.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, over and above what is usual.

clue.text: Pal packing revolutionary weapon

indicators.note: packing means holding inside, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a mate is a pal
Che Guevara was the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.surface: A friend carrying a weapon fit for a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packing' also means carrying a gun, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy knife used as a tool and weapon.

clue.text: Question in church about acceptable fruit

indicators.note: the first group of letters is wrapped around the next piece, as if it were about it

parts.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England
U means upper-class, hence socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Someone asks, during a service, whether a certain fruit is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes Q-IN-CE go round U (upper-class, so acceptable), placing it just after the Q.
explanation.definitionFit: The quince is a hard yellow pear-shaped fruit, used for jelly and preserves.

clue.text: Make-up of Universal screening 'ET'?

indicators.note: screening means hiding behind or around, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: cosmic means relating to the whole universe
taken as written: the film alien's initials

explanation.surface: A question about the make-up artistry in Universal's screening of the film ET.
explanation.walkthrough: Universal Pictures released ET, so 'screening' reads as showing a film; here it means hiding, one piece enclosing the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetics are beauty products, which is what make-up is; here the adjective doubles as a noun.

clue.text: Flight of rocket with this person wearing space body suit

parts.note: to rocket is to rise rapidly, as prices spiral

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a star is a body in space
the setter refers to themself as I
a suit is a legal case

explanation.surface: An astronaut in a space suit boards a rocket for its flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' and 'rocket' suggest space travel, but a flight here is a set of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a set of stairs, and a spiral staircase winds round a central column.

clue.text: Refined fare tons put on cereal abroad

indicators.note: in a down clue, put on means placed above, so the letter comes first
abroad in the sense of astray or all over the place signals rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: Fancy food piles tons of weight onto foreign breakfast cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is syrup produced in sugar refining, so it is a refined foodstuff.

clue.text: Troublemaker on the Spanish force

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous troublemaker
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A mischief-maker sits atop the Spanish armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel someone is to drive or compel them to act.

clue.text: Bond character that starts a pyramid scheme?

parts.note: a chain is a bond that holds
a letter is a character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A James Bond villain who launches a fraudulent pyramid scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Chain letters ask recipients to send money on to others, the classic way to begin a pyramid swindle.

clue.text: Line in funny gag

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the longer word

parts.note: funny in the sense of odd means strange

explanation.surface: A comedian slips a line into an amusing joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gag' reads as a joke, alongside 'funny', but here it is the verb meaning to choke.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag someone can mean to choke or throttle them, cutting off breath and speech.

clue.text: Enthusiasm one may see blow over

parts.note: a gust is a blow of wind
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Excitement that a person expects to fade quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto means hearty relish or zest for doing something.

clue.text: One going into town for fish?

indicators.note: going into means entering, so the numeral is put inside

parts.note: a town is a place
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone heads into town to buy fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a flat sea fish common in British fish shops.

clue.text: Two chapters about a very loud and popular bird

indicators.note: the two chapter abbreviations sit about the rest, one at each end

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for chapter, here taken twice
the second CH of the pair
FF, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: Two book chapters on a noisy, much-loved bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The chaffinch is a common European finch with a pinkish breast.

clue.text: Common sense shown by British artist? In spades

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: A British artist shows plenty of good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In spades' looks like the idiom for 'abundantly', but it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Brains is an informal word for intelligence or good practical judgement.

clue.text: Pantomime character, stooge on stage at the start

parts.note: a stooge is the butt of jokes
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A comic sidekick takes the stage at the beginning of a panto.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show; Buttons is Cinderella's loyal page boy in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttons is a stock role, the servant who befriends the heroine in Cinderella pantomimes.

clue.text: Fresh and clear schedule of events

indicators.note: fresh suggests something new, so these letters are made anew in another order

explanation.surface: A plea for a new, uncluttered programme of happenings.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar is a list of dates with their planned engagements, as in a social calendar.

clue.text: As with a bareknuckle boxer, play hardball?

definitions.meaning: a bareknuckle fighter literally fights with no gloves on
to play hardball is to act ruthlessly, as when one announces the fight is now in earnest

explanation.surface: Comparing a tough negotiator to a fighter without gloves.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hostilities have begun in earnest; taken literally, it describes a fighter whose hands are bare.

clue.text: Check out organ at university

parts.note: the eye is an organ of sight
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A medical inspection of an organ at a university hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye up is to look at someone or something appraisingly, informally to check out.

clue.text: Freeloader in shelter? Check

parts.note: lee is shelter from the wind
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether a scrounger is in the hostel.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is someone who lives off others, a parasite.

clue.text: One exercising veto by right?

indicators.note: exercising suggests working something over and moving it about, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A citizen using a power of refusal as their entitlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercising' signals that the four letters of the clue's veto are shuffled into the act of casting a ballot, before the abbreviation for right is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone casting a ballot can reject a proposal, using their democratic right.

clue.text: More than enough beer member's got in

indicators.note: got in means admitted inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP has brought in plenty of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful, sufficient with some to spare.

clue.text: Savoury dish: ingredients in welcome letter

indicators.note: the ingredients are what is contained in a mixture, so the letters inside the phrase are taken

explanation.surface: A recipe for a savoury dish arrives in a friendly note.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette is beaten eggs cooked in a pan, often with savoury fillings.

clue.text: Very strong, round number in gym

indicators.note: the other pieces are placed inside the two letters for gym

parts.note: PT, physical training, is gym class
O is round in shape
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A very strong person does a round of reps in the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: Potent means powerful or forceful, as with a potent drink or argument.

clue.text: A gem may be gleaned from his paper

indicators.note: gleaned suggests picking things up and gathering them into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jewel story might be picked up from a man's newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapphire is a precious stone, typically blue, a variety of corundum.

clue.text: Crude burrow close to spinney

parts.note: an earth is a fox's burrow

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A rough hole dug near a small wood.
explanation.walkthrough: A spinney is a small wood or copse, a common British word.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse or crude, unrefined and down to earth.
